title: billing-attribution-and-throttle-remediation-notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects UX notes, wireframe ideas, and an initial backlog for a unified view that ties per-key / per-route usage to billing attribution and automated throttle remediation. Goal is to make it fast for an engineer or SRE to: 1) identify which credential/route is causing unexpected spend/latency, 2) confirm impact with lightweight investigation tools, and 3) apply a safe remediation (throttle, fallback, or billing alert) with an auditable trail.

Background / problem statements (tl;dr):
- Teams see spikes in per-key spend and have trouble mapping token counts to real traffic patterns (bursts vs sustained).
- Current console surfaces usage charts and quotas separately; customers want a single surface that shows usage -> cost -> control actions.
- Support frequently intervenes by temporary throttles; we need a safer self-serve experience and a clear audit trail.

Primary personas:
- Platform engineer (implements safeguards; needs bulk actions and CSV exports)
- Product engineer (troubleshoots a single key/route quickly)
- Finance/ops reviewer (validates billing anomalies; needs clear attribution)
- Support/CS (applies emergency throttles and documents runbook steps)

High-level goals:
- Surface per-key and per-route spend attribution (tokens -> cost) with 3x time granularity (1h, 6h, 24h) and the ability to toggle lookback windows.
- Provide a ‘Remediation’ panel with safe defaults: soft-throttle (percentage), hard-throttle (requests/min), fallback route, model downgrade, and automated rollback.
- Keep an auditable action log with reason, actor, and rollback/expiry.
- Exportable incident bundle (CSV + snapshot) for finance and postmortem.

Key success metrics (initial):
- Time to identify root credential/route reduced from median 45m -> 10m.
- % of throttle actions performed via console (vs support ticket) increased to >60% for customers on Dedicated.
- Reduction in customer-reported billing surprises by 30% in 3 months.

Wireframe components (sketch-level descriptions):
1) Overview header (top row)
   - Quick KPI tiles: "Active keys with over-threshold spend", "Total incr. vs baseline (24h)", "Open throttles".
   - Datepicker + granularity toggle (hour/6h/day).

2) Split main area (left: explorer, right: action/detail)
   LEFT: Usage explorer (drill-first)
     - Stacked area chart (token consumption by route stacked by credential) with hover drill showing exact token counts and cost estimate per point.
     - Mini heatmap below showing distribution of requests by hour-of-day x route (cells sized by tokens).
     - Search/filter bar: by credential id, route, model family, tag, region.

   RIGHT: Focus pane (selected key/route)
     - Summary card: key metadata (owner, create date, billing tier, tags), 24h token total, estimated cost, anomaly flag.
     - Attribution timeline: small sparkline of token->cost and events (deploys, config changes, rollouts pulled from linked artifacts).
     - Quick actions (primary): "Soft throttle 50% for 30m", "Set hard limit: 200 r/min", "Fallback to smaller model", "Create cost alert". Each action opens a minimal confirm sheet with recommended reason and auto-generated runbook note.
     - Advanced actions: bulk edit across multiple keys, schedule throttle windows, save remediation template.

3) Remediation flows (UX notes):
   - Default safety: all throttle actions are non-destructive by default (soft throttle first), require a short justification text, and auto-expire after chosen duration.
   - Two-step confirm for hard throttles (to avoid accidental outages).
   - Preview impact modal: estimate percent cost reduction and expected latency change (rough), based on model of past efficiency and prefix cache ratio.
   - Auto-rollback: option to auto-rollback based on spike reduction or after N minutes if downstream error rates spike.

4) Incident bundle export
   - Button on focus pane: "Export incident bundle" produces: CSV (per-request aggregates), JSON snapshot (console view), and recommended notes for billing ops.
   - CSV schema (draft) columns: [timestamp_hour, credential_id, route, model_family, tokens_in, tokens_out, estimated_cost_usd, region, request_count, avg_latency_ms, anomaly_score, linked_deploy_id]

Flows / example scenarios (short):
- Scenario A: Burst of tokens from a misconfigured client SDK
Steps: 1) Search by credential id -> heatmap shows a concentrated spike at 09:12. 2) Focus pane shows recent deploy for route; anomaly flag true. 3) Click "Soft throttle 60% for 1h" -> confirmation + auto-generated runbook note attached to key. 4) Export incident bundle and attach to ticket.

- Scenario B: Sustained slow leak causing month-end bill surprise
Steps: 1) Finance flags unexpected charge; open console -> top KPI tile shows unusual sustained spend. 2) Use filter to find keys with >X% increase vs baseline. 3) Pull CSV export and map to invoices for reconciliation. 4) Create permanent quota fence (requires support approval for some enterprise tiers).

Backlog (prioritized, rough estimates):
- M1 (2w): Instrument front-end charts with token->cost mapping and hover details. Owner: Evan. Ticket: ENG-2971.
- M2 (3w): Focus pane metadata card + simple soft-throttle action (backend API + audit log). Owner: Jonas.
- M3 (2w): Heatmap and CSV export for incident bundle. Owner: Priya.
- M4 (4w): Preview impact modal + auto-rollback rules (requires simulation model). Owner: Lena.
- M5 (3w): Permissions & approval flows for hard throttles (enterprise). Owner: Product-ops.
- M6 (ongoing): UX polish and microcopy review; measure usage and iterate.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Cost model accuracy: do we use hourly average unit cost per model variant or compute from raw infra metrics? (Ops + Finance input required)
- Throttle semantics: do we expose percent-of-requests or target RPS? both? initial MVP should expose percent and hard RPS limit.
- Audit retention policy: how long do we keep runbook notes and exports (default 90 days vs enterprise configurable).
- Mapping of linked artifacts: what events do we surface automatically (deploys from GitHub, rollout events, support tickets)?

Microcopy / tooltip suggestions (quick):
- Soft throttle: "Reduce request volume gradually; non-permanent, auto-expire option"
- Hard throttle: "Block incoming requests above limit — use with caution. Requires two-step confirmation."
- Preview impact: "Estimated reduction in tokens and cost based on last 24h of traffic. Not guaranteed."

Operational concerns (notes to infra team):
- Need a low-latency path for throttle actions to reach edge routers (<5s target) and an idempotent API.
- Ensure audit log writes are transactional with action execution to avoid orphaned actions.
- Add feature flag to turn on/off auto-rollback heuristics per customer.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Sync with infra (Evan/Jonas) to size the soft-throttle API + audit log work (this week).
2) Run a quick study with Finance to decide billing attribution model (next week).
3) Design: create two high-fidelity wireframes from this doc (focus pane + full-screen explorer) and run 30-min usability with 3 internal SREs.
4) Prepare a small alpha release for a subset of Dedicated customers (opt-in) to gather early feedback.

Notes to self / rough ideas (brainstorm):
- Consider an "investigation mode" timeline where admins can scrub forward/backward to simulate throttle impact on historical data.
- Alert-to-runbook mapping: when an alert fires, console suggests a pre-populated remediation template.
- Ability to pin a key to a watchlist with anomaly alerts and suggested thresholds auto-suggested by our model.

References / links:
- See ENG-2971 for front-end chart work and initial spike detection hook.
- Throttle runbook examples: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Throttle+Runbooks

-- end --
